Subject: Questions on MSA redline (output / training rights)

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and legal reviewed the draft MSA and attached a redline (attached PDF). Two items they asked to confirm:

1) Output assignment — the redline currently requests explicit assignment of "Product Output" for downstream commercialization. Can Redwood confirm whether we can accept any assignment language at all, or only a limited license?

2) Training & telemetry — we need clarity on whether NovaHealth data or derived outputs may be used to improve models or telemetry datasets. The redline proposes a narrow exception for aggregated telemetry only and a separate clause allowing training if we opt in later.

We can be flexible but want to capture the path forward in the MSA so our security/compliance folks have clear boundaries. Attaching the redline for your legal team.

Can we schedule a short sync tomorrow to walk through the redline?

Appreciate it,
Kate
Procurement Manager — NovaHealth

Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA redline (output / training rights)

Kate —

Thanks for sending the redline and the clear asks. Quick answers up front:
- Assignment: Redwood's standard position is to grant an exclusive, perpetual license to use service outputs as part of the customer product; we do not transfer model IP nor generally accept full assignment of Redwood-owned model improvements.
- Training & telemetry: We can agree to an "aggregated telemetry only" clause (operational metrics and anonymized usage signals) and to an opt-in path for training on customer data, subject to a separate addendum and additional security/controls.

I'm looping in Markus from Legal and Neha from AM to propose concrete language and walk through the redline with you. We can do a 30 minute call tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT if that works.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on MSA redline (output / training rights)

Kate / Grace —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed NovaHealth's redline and sketched preferred counter-language below. High level: we will not assign Redwood core model IP or model weights. We can offer a clear, customer-friendly license pathway for outputs and a two-track approach for training: telemetry-only by default, training-on-customer-data only by explicit opt-in and additional SOW or addendum. Suggested text snippets follow — please treat as working language we can put into a clean redline: 

1) Product Output / License
"Customer shall have a perpetual, worldwide, transferable, royalty-free license to use, reproduce, distribute and create derivative products from Customer Data Outputs generated by the Service solely in connection with Customer's internal operations and its downstream products; Redwood retains ownership of the Service and underlying model weights and any improvements thereto unless separately agreed in writing."

2) Telemetry & Aggregated Metrics
"Redwood may collect aggregated usage telemetry and operational metadata for the purposes of service improvement, monitoring, and capacity planning. Such telemetry shall be de-identified and shall not include PII or Customer Data. Redwood shall not use Customer Data or Customer Data Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve any model used to serve other customers without Customer's prior written opt-in via an agreed addendum."

3) Training Opt-in Addendum
"If Customer chooses to opt into data-based training, the parties will execute a Training Addendum that describes data scoping, retention, access controls, audit rights, and compensation. Training Addendum execution will require signoff from both parties' security and legal teams."

I recommend we propose the snippets above and ask NovaHealth to confirm whether the assignment language they added is narrow (product output vs. Redwood model IP). I also suggest we prepare a short summary (1 page) that explains the opt-in path for training, the expected timeline and security controls. Olga, can you draft the one-pager outlining telemetry-only vs training-addendum flow? Neha, please coordinate a 30-min demo with Kate if they want a call tomorrow morning.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_summary_notes.docx (summary of suggested language)

From: Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@novahealth.com>

Cc: Kate Lin <kate.lin@novahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA redline (output / training rights)

Markus —

Appreciate the quick read. A couple of clarifying points from NovaHealth legal: 
- The assignment language in our PDF was intended to guarantee NovaHealth can commercialize derivative products built from the outputs; it was not meant to take ownership of Redwood models. If you can accept a broad commercial license for outputs (perpetual, transferable, commercial), we can remove the assignment request.
- On telemetry: NovaHealth needs an explicit carveout that telemetry excludes payloads (raw prompts and completions) unless explicitly agreed; aggregated metrics are okay.

We like the opt-in addendum approach for training provided the addendum includes audit rights and a firm timeline for data deletion from training datasets. Can you confirm Redwood's standard retention window for telemetry and whether we can negotiate a shorter window for NovaHealth?

If you can share the one-pager and a proposed redline turn-around, we'll update our PDF and aim to get Legal sign-off within the week.

Thanks,
Derek Shaw
Sr. Director, Product — NovaHealth

Derek / Kate —

Great progress — thank you. Quick next steps we agreed internally and want to confirm with you: 
1) We'll accept removing assignment in favor of a perpetual, worldwide commercial license for Customer Outputs (language based on Markus's snippet).
2) Telemetry: Redwood will limit collection to de-identified aggregated metrics by default; payloads (prompts/completions) will not be used for training or shared externally without explicit opt-in. Standard telemetry retention is 12 months; NovaHealth can request a 90-day retention carveout tied to their account settings — we'll note that in the addendum.
3) Training: we'll prepare a Training Addendum template (scope + security + deletion timeline + compensation). Execution requires signoff from both security teams.
4) Deliverables: Markus/Olga will drop the one-page summary and a tracked-change MSA counter (clean redline) by EOD Monday. Neha will book a 30-minute call for Tue 9/14 to walk through any remaining items.

If that aligns with NovaHealth, Kate, please confirm and we'll proceed.

Thanks — talk soon.
